literal: With justice, virtue having practiced, usefulness those who possess, their noble character will praise the world.
translation: The world praises the noble character of those who make themselves useful to others by practicing justice and virtue.
modern: நீதியோடும் நன்மையோடும் பிறருக்குப் பயன்படும் நற்செயல்களைச் செய்கின்றவர்களுடைய நற்பண்பை உலகத்தார் போற்றுவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet explains whose character is worthy of global appreciation. The poet uses 'nayan' to mean justice or propriety, and 'naṉṟi' to mean virtue or benevolence. When a person combines these two qualities to become 'payaṉ uṭaiyār'—someone whose life is of practical benefit to society—their behavior is recognized as true 'paṇpu' (noble character). The world ('ulaku', representing the wise people of the world) will naturally praise and celebrate such individuals.
